chunks: By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever's two days are equal is at a loss; whoever's latter day is the worse of the two is cursed;
whoever does not recognize improvement in himself is closer to decline; and whoever is closer to decline, then death is better for him than life.

key_terms.الزيادة: Ziyadah: increase, growth, improvement - referring to advancement in faith and virtue
key_terms.النقصان: Nuqsan: decrease, decline, deterioration - the opposite of spiritual growth
key_terms.مغبون: Magbun: deceived or at a loss, one who has been cheated in a transaction - here metaphorically indicating spiritual loss from wasting time
key_terms.ملعون: Mal'un: cursed or removed from God's mercy - a severe warning against regression

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about self-improvement and wasting time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a powerful exhortation on the imperative of continuous self-improvement. Addressed to the faithful gathered in the assembly of Sheikh al-Saduq in 368 AH, this teaching establishes a graduated scale: stagnation is a spiritual loss, regression is a curse, and the failure to pursue growth leads one closer to ruin. The hadith reflects a core Islamic ethical principle that a believer must constantly advance in knowledge, piety, and good deeds.
